problem: build_gantt.py opened with a single-quoted multi-line string, so importing it from build_matrices.py raised SyntaxError and the 'Build matrices from authority files' step exited 1 (run 42553625095).
failed_approach: Trusting the write_file ok=true receipt as proof the Python source parses; the receipt proves the blob landed, not that it is valid Python.
lesson: A new module imported by build_matrices must start with a real docstring or comment, and its first proof is the build step conclusion on the following push run - not the write receipt.
resolution: Docstring edit at 96ef7894 produced green run 42554257008.

problem: 'Commit regenerated matrices' exited 1 at 42553597443, which I initially attributed to an unguarded commit on a clean tree.
failed_approach: Diagnosing the failing step from its name instead of reading the step body; the workflow at 3fc6c647 already wraps commit/push in an `if git diff --cached --quiet` guard.
lesson: Read the workflow step body before proposing a workflow repair. When the guard is already present, a step-7 exit 1 means the else-branch ran and the commit or push itself failed, so look at tree state and remote head at that commit rather than rewriting the guard.
correction: Misdiagnosis corrected; no workflow change required for this id.

problem: Unauthenticated job pages return 'This step has been truncated due to its large size' for every step, so the failing log line is never visible.
failed_approach: Trying to read the cause from the job HTML page.
lesson: Use run_jobs step conclusions plus the annotation list (which names the step and 'Process completed with exit code 1'); never quote a log line that was not actually returned.

problem: The workflow's own 'Commit regenerated matrices' step pushes a commit, so the branch head no longer matches the sha the proven check-run covers. It pushed 187168f5 earlier and 60b4d6cc after run 42556696754, while that run's check-run head_sha stayed e3eba97e.
failed_approach: Treating a green run on the branch as sufficient for the merge gate, or assuming branch_head stays at the last file I wrote.
lesson: Before merge_pr, take branch_head and the branch run list in the same turn and match run.sha to the exact head. A green run whose sha is an ancestor does not authorize the merge.

problem: Head 60b4d6cc, created by the workflow's own commit step, has no workflow run in the branch run list, so the exact-head check requirement can never be met by polling.
failed_approach: Polling branch_head plus runs repeatedly and waiting for a run whose sha equals the self-commit head.
lesson: A commit pushed by a workflow step with the default GITHUB_TOKEN does not trigger a new workflow run. To get a check at a stable head, push one allowed-path change yourself; once generated outputs are already committed the run's guarded commit step produces no diff and the head stays put.

problem: PROGRESS.json under docs/venice-audit-v1/ is rewritten by the build step, so authored text there does not survive and editing it re-fires the guarded commit.
failed_approach: Planning to force a fresh push run by editing docs/venice-audit-v1/PROGRESS.json, assuming my write would define the new head content.
lesson: Distinguish authored files from build outputs before choosing a push target. My PROGRESS.json write became 4b8c54ff, but head 60b4d6cc replaced it with b3c23c40. Force runs from a filtered path the build never writes: tests/test_repo_requirements_audit.py or the workflow file.
